rounds.text: Shanti Gold International Ltd trades at an attractive valuation with a P/E of 14.8 [E1] and a lower multiple of 12.48x compared to the sector benchmark of 23.72x [E5], alongside an EV/EBITDA of 9.03x that beats the sector's 13.71x [E10]. The company exhibits exceptional capital efficiency, boasting an ROA of 21.76% [E7], an ROE of 23.42% [E8], and an ROCE of 24.85% [E9], all significantly outperforming their respective sector benchmarks. Fundamental strength is further backed by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value pointing to a 27.1% margin of safety [E18, E19] and a reverse DCF showing the current price only prices in a modest 5.7% growth against the 10.0% base case [E20]. Operational tailwinds are firmly in place, highlighted by management maintaining a strong revenue guidance target of INR3,500 crores for the year [E44] supported by volume growth expectations of 30% to 40% and value growth of 50% to 60% [E43], a newly commissioned facility in Marol [E48], and an upcoming Jaipur facility backed by a INR47 crores capex investment [E49]. Conceded: promoter holding decreased by 4.54 percentage points to 70.35% [E14], foreign institutional holding dropped to 2.22% [E15], and domestic institutional holding declined to 1.64% [E16].

The bear case rests on notable insider and institutional divestment alongside elevated valuation risks compared to the broader sector [E6, E14, E15, E16]. Promoter holding dropped from 74.89% in September 2025 to 70.35% in September 2026, marking a meaningful 4.54 percentage point reduction [E14], while domestic institutional ownership sharply contracted from 4.01% to 1.64% and foreign institutional holdings declined to 2.22% over the same period [E15, E16]. Furthermore, the stock trades at a price-to-book ratio of 3.33x, which significantly outpaces the sector benchmark of 1.94x [E6], pointing to a rich valuation that leaves little margin for operational missteps. Compounding these risks, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3] and carries an annualised volatility of 58.5% [E27], exposing investors to substantial price swings without immediate cash flow returns. Conceded: the company displays strong returns on capital and equity outperforming sector benchmarks, alongside a positive DCF margin of safety [E7, E8, E9, E19]. Operational headwinds are further underscored by historical reliance on volatile gold pricing that previously forced the company to temporarily step back from Gold Metal Loans [E61], coupled with subdued demand periods reported during May and June [E60].

Conceded: promoter holding dropped by 4.54 percentage points to 70.35% and institutional holdings contracted [E14, E15, E16]. However, this institutional divestment is directly contradicted by current scanX signal data showing positive institutional money flow with a holding increase of 0.36 percentage points [E17]. While the price-to-book ratio sits at 3.33x against a sector benchmark of 1.94x [E6], this premium valuation is fully justified by elite operational returns, including an ROA of 21.76%, ROE of 23.42%, and ROCE of 24.85% that heavily outperform sector benchmarks [E7, E8, E9]. Furthermore, the bear's focus on a 0.00% dividend yield [E3] ignores the aggressive capital reinvestment driving a projected 50% to 60% value growth target and a top-line revenue guidance of INR3,500 crores [E44, E64]. Conceded: the company offers no immediate cash return [E3] and carries 58.5% annualized volatility [E27], yet the discounted cash flow model establishes a robust 27.1% margin of safety against intrinsic value [E19]. Finally, historical adjustments regarding Gold Metal Loans [E61] are overshadowed by the successful commissioning of the Marol facility and ongoing expansion at Jaipur designed to capture massive domestic and export demand [E46, E48, E49].

Conceded: scanX shows positive money flow with a holding change of +0.36 percentage points [E17], but this minor uptick does not erase the broader, structural institutional retreat where foreign institutions dropped to 2.22% and domestic institutions fell to 1.64% year-over-year [E15, E16]. Furthermore, the bull's dismissal of the 3.33x price-to-book premium over the 1.94x sector benchmark ignores the tangible risk that this valuation prices in perfection, leaving no cushion if the aggressive 50% to 60% value growth and INR3,500 crore revenue targets falter [E6, E44, E64]. Conceded: a DCF model calculates a 27.1% margin of safety [E19], yet that theoretical margin offers little comfort alongside a punishing 58.5% annualized volatility and a historical worst drawdown of -38.1% [E22, E27]. The bull's defense of capital reinvestment bypasses the plain fact of a 0.00% dividend yield alongside shrinking promoter ownership, which declined significantly by 4.54 percentage points to 70.35% [E3, E14]. Finally, while new facilities in Marol and Jaipur are cited as growth catalysts [E48, E49], management itself acknowledged subdued demand during May and June alongside historical exits from Gold Metal Loans due to high price volatility [E60, E61].

Conceded: promoter holding declined by 4.54 percentage points [E14], and annualized volatility sits at 58.5% with a historical drawdown of -38.1% [E22, E27]. However, the bear's alarm over institutional retreat ignores the active positive money flow showing a holding increase of +0.36 percentage points [E17], countering the annualized institutional comparison. The critique of the 3.33x price-to-book ratio [E6] ignores the company's superior return metrics, including an ROA of 21.76% and ROCE of 24.85% that comfortably crush sector benchmarks of 4.96% and 10.39% [E7, E9]. Furthermore, while management noted subdued demand in May and June alongside historical adjustments to Gold Metal Loans [E60, E61], these are balanced by robust operational expansion with the Marol facility commencement and the upcoming Jaipur plant [E48, E49], backed by strong relative-strength ratings of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E24]. Finally, the DCF model's 27.1% margin of safety and reverse DCF requiring only a modest 5.7% earnings growth provide a solid mathematical anchor against valuation anxieties [E18, E19, E20].

Conceded: [E17] shows positive institutional money flow with a holding change of +0.36 percentage points. However, this minor quarterly uptick does not erase the broader, structural institutional retreat where domestic institutions slashed their stake from 4.01% to 1.64% and foreign institutions fell from 2.68% to 2.22% year-over-year [E15, E16], nor does it offset the promoter dilution of 4.54 percentage points [E14, E31]. While the bull champions the company's return metrics [E7, E9], the price-to-book ratio sits at an inflated 3.33x compared to a sector benchmark of just 1.94x [E6], indicating that these returns are heavily priced in. Furthermore, the bull's dismissal of demand headwinds is unconvincing given that management explicitly conceded subdued demand during May and June alongside historical retreats from Gold Metal Loans due to high volatility [E60, E61]. The reliance on a stellar relative-strength rating and projected facility expansions [E24, E48, E49] ignores the extreme annualised volatility of 58.5% and a track record of 0.00% dividend yield [E3, E27], leaving equity holders entirely exposed to price fluctuations without regular cash returns.
